item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is inviting qualified professionals to apply for an exciting Online Volunteer Opportunity in Grant and Proposal Development Support with its Eswatini Country Office. This 12-week virtual assignment offers an opportunity to contribute to the work of a United Nations agency while supporting resource mobilization, strategic partnerships, grant writing, donor intelligence, and programme development.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals with experience in grant writing, international development, resource mobilization, technical proposal development, and donor relations. The selected volunteer will work remotely with UNFPA Eswatini’s programme team, helping strengthen the organization’s ability to secure funding and expand programmes addressing sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), gender-based violence (GBV), adolescent health, and youth empowerment.

With a commitment of approximately 16–20 hours per week, this assignment provides an opportunity to gain practical experience working with a UN agency, contribute to meaningful development initiatives, and strengthen professional skills in international development and resource mobilization.

About the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)

The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is the United Nations agency responsible for promoting sexual and reproductive health and rights worldwide. Its mission is to build a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled.

UNFPA works with governments, civil society organizations, development partners, and international institutions to advance reproductive health, gender equality, population data, and the rights and well-being of women, girls, adolescents, and young people.

Through its country offices and global partnerships, UNFPA supports programmes that address critical development challenges, including maternal mortality, teenage pregnancy, gender-based violence, harmful practices, and unequal access to sexual and reproductive health services.

The UNFPA Eswatini Country Office works closely with the Government of Eswatini and other development partners to advance national priorities related to sexual and reproductive health, adolescent and youth empowerment, gender equality, and population data.

This online volunteer assignment will contribute to these objectives by strengthening the office’s resource mobilization efforts, improving the quality of funding proposals, and identifying opportunities to establish strategic partnerships with international donors and funding institutions.

Overview of the UNFPA Eswatini Online Volunteer Opportunity

The Grant and Proposal Development Support assignment is designed to support UNFPA Eswatini in developing competitive funding proposals, identifying potential donors, and strengthening communication materials used to attract financial support for its development programmes.

The selected online volunteer will collaborate virtually with the UNFPA Eswatini Programme Specialist for SRHR/HIV and the Officer-in-Charge, alongside programme teams responsible for different development priorities.

The assignment will run for 12 weeks and require approximately 16–20 hours of work per week. As an online assignment, the volunteer will perform all responsibilities remotely rather than relocating to Eswatini.

Key details of the opportunity include:

  • Host Organization: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA).
  • Host Country: Eswatini.
  • Assignment Title: Grant and Proposal Development Support.
  • Opportunity Modality: Online.
  • Assignment Duration: 12 weeks.
  • Working Hours: 16–20 hours per week.
  • Number of Available Positions: 1.
  • Recruitment Type: Competitive recruitment.
  • Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals.
  • Required Language: English (Fluent).
  • Application Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 03:00.

Background and Context of the Assignment

UNFPA Eswatini operates in a development environment where sustained financial support and strong institutional partnerships are essential to addressing significant social and public health challenges.

The country continues to experience challenges related to teenage pregnancy, gender-based violence, and limited access to youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services. These challenges particularly affect adolescents, young people, and marginalized communities, highlighting the importance of targeted development programmes and sustainable funding.

To address these challenges, UNFPA Eswatini is implementing its 2026–2030 Country Programme, which aligns with national development priorities, the Sustainable Development Goals, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).

The programme focuses on several important priorities:

1. Strengthening Sexual and Reproductive Health Services

One of the major priorities is improving systems that deliver high-quality sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services and commodities, particularly for adolescents and young people.

This includes supporting access to essential health services, addressing barriers to reproductive healthcare, and improving the availability of youth-friendly services.

2. Addressing Gender and Social Inequalities

UNFPA also seeks to address multidimensional inequalities, particularly those resulting from gender-related, sociocultural, and economic barriers.

Special attention is given to rural communities, where harmful gender stereotypes and unequal opportunities can prevent women and girls from accessing essential services and exercising their rights.

3. Improving Population Data and Evidence-Based Programming

Another priority involves addressing population data gaps through improved data analysis and investment in disaggregated information.

Reliable data enables development organizations and policymakers to identify vulnerable populations, understand inequalities, and design targeted interventions that respond to actual community needs.

4. Strengthening Strategic Partnerships and Resource Mobilization

Achieving these objectives requires sustainable financial resources and strong partnerships with international development institutions, bilateral donors, corporate foundations, and other funding organizations.

The online volunteer will contribute directly to this priority by helping UNFPA identify funding opportunities, develop persuasive proposals, and improve its donor engagement strategies.

Roles and Responsibilities of the Selected Online Volunteer

The selected volunteer will undertake responsibilities across three major areas: grant and proposal writing, donor intelligence and strategy support, and strategic communications.

1. Grant and Proposal Writing

A significant part of the assignment will involve preparing and improving funding proposals designed to attract support from international donors and development partners.

The volunteer will be expected to undertake the following responsibilities:

Drafting Funding Proposals

The volunteer will lead the structural development of competitive concept notes and comprehensive project proposals.

These proposals will be tailored to the requirements and priorities of different funding institutions, including:

  • Global thematic funding mechanisms.
  • Bilateral development agencies.
  • Corporate foundations.
  • International development funding organizations.

The objective is to develop persuasive proposals that clearly communicate the challenges facing communities in Eswatini, the proposed interventions, expected results, and the resources required to implement them.

Developing Logical Frameworks and Theories of Change

The volunteer will support the development of Results-Based Management (RBM) frameworks, logical frameworks (log frames), indicator-tracking mechanisms, and Theories of Change (ToC).

These tools are essential for designing development projects and demonstrating how proposed activities will lead to measurable outcomes.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Developing logical frameworks that connect project activities with expected outputs and outcomes.
  • Identifying appropriate performance indicators.
  • Establishing mechanisms for tracking project progress.
  • Formulating Theories of Change that explain how proposed interventions will generate meaningful development results.
  • Ensuring that project frameworks are consistent with specific donor requirements.

Integrating Data and Evidence into Proposals

Strong funding proposals require reliable evidence that demonstrates the importance of the proposed intervention.

The volunteer will synthesize relevant Eswatini country data, particularly information concerning:

  • Adolescent and teenage pregnancy rates.
  • Gender-based violence (GBV) incidence.
  • Access to sexual and reproductive health services.
  • Youth health service accessibility.
  • Development challenges affecting marginalized communities.

This information will be used to develop convincing investment rationales that demonstrate why particular programmes deserve financial support.

Reviewing and Editing Proposal Documents

The volunteer will also provide editorial support and quality assurance for proposals, concept notes, and donor presentation materials prepared by the UNFPA Country Office.

This responsibility involves reviewing documents to ensure:

  • Clear and professional writing.
  • Logical organization and consistency.
  • Strong arguments supported by evidence.
  • Alignment with UNFPA programme priorities.
  • Compliance with donor-specific requirements.
  • High-quality presentation and communication.

2. Donor Intelligence and Strategy Support

The second major responsibility involves researching funding institutions, identifying potential donors, and analyzing changes in international development financing.

This work will help UNFPA Eswatini identify funding opportunities that align with its programme priorities.

Donor Mapping and Database Development

The volunteer will research and maintain a database of potential donors and funding institutions relevant to UNFPA’s work in Eswatini.

The database will include information such as:

  • Donor funding priorities.
  • Eligibility requirements for funding applications.
  • Application and call-for-proposal cycles.
  • Geographic funding allocations.
  • Relevant thematic funding opportunities.
  • Potential opportunities for collaboration and strategic partnerships.

This information will help the Country Office develop a more organized and effective approach to resource mobilization.

Monitoring Global and Regional Funding Trends

The volunteer will monitor developments in international development financing, particularly changes in official development assistance (ODA) and donor priorities.

The objective is to identify emerging funding opportunities that could support UNFPA’s work.

Areas of interest include:

  • Climate change adaptation.
  • Sexual and reproductive health and rights.
  • Gender equality and women’s empowerment.
  • Youth development.
  • Public health and population development.

By understanding changing donor priorities, UNFPA will be better positioned to identify relevant funding opportunities and adapt its proposals to emerging development needs.

Ensuring Strategic Alignment

Another important responsibility is verifying that funding proposals and related documents align with the strategic frameworks guiding UNFPA’s operations in Eswatini.

The volunteer will ensure that proposal materials reflect:

  • The UNFPA 8th Eswatini Country Programme Document (2026–2030).
  • The United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).
  • Relevant national health policies.
  • Sexual and reproductive health and rights policies.
  • Gender-based violence prevention frameworks.
  • Youth development policies and guidelines.

This alignment is important because funding proposals must demonstrate how proposed projects contribute to established development priorities.

3. Strategic Communications and Donor Stewardship

The third area of responsibility focuses on developing professional communication materials that help UNFPA present its programmes and funding priorities to potential donors and development partners.

Developing Donor Pitch Decks and Presentation Materials

The volunteer will conceptualize and prepare professional donor pitch decks, operational briefing sheets, and executive summary documents.

These materials will communicate important information about UNFPA’s programmes and investment opportunities.

They should clearly present:

  • Programme objectives and priorities.
  • Development challenges being addressed.
  • Proposed interventions.
  • Expected outputs and outcomes.
  • Investment requirements.
  • Anticipated development impact.

These materials will support resource mobilization activities and high-level engagement with potential donors and institutional partners.

Reviewing Donor Reports

The volunteer will also assist in reviewing and editing important donor reporting packages.

This includes checking the structure, clarity, visual presentation, and overall quality of reports before they are submitted to funding institutions.

The objective is to ensure that reporting documents meet donor expectations and communicate programme achievements, results, and implementation progress effectively.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Applicants interested in the UNFPA Grant and Proposal Development Support opportunity should possess relevant academic qualifications, professional experience, and technical competencies.

The host organization is particularly interested in candidates who can independently develop high-quality proposals, conduct donor research, and contribute to international development programmes.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree in one of the following fields or a closely related social science discipline:

  • International Relations.
  • Development Studies.
  • Public Health.
  • Gender Studies.
  • Public Administration.
  • Economics.
  • Related social science fields.

A relevant academic background will help applicants understand development policies, international cooperation, public health challenges, and the institutional frameworks involved in resource mobilization.

Required Professional Experience

Candidates should demonstrate previous experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Grant writing.
  • Technical proposal development.
  • Institutional resource mobilization.
  • Donor relations management.

Experience in these areas is important because the volunteer will be expected to contribute to actual proposal development and donor engagement activities.

Additional Experience Considered an Advantage

Although not necessarily mandatory, previous experience in the following thematic areas will be highly valued:

Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights: Experience working on projects involving reproductive health, adolescent health, sexual health education, or access to healthcare services.

Youth Development: Familiarity with programmes supporting youth empowerment, adolescent development, and opportunities for young people.

Gender Equality: Experience with initiatives addressing gender inequality, women’s rights, gender-based violence, and women’s empowerment.

Demographic Data Infrastructure: Experience working with population data, demographic research, data analysis, or evidence-based development programming.

Experience collaborating with United Nations agencies, multilateral institutions, or international non-governmental organizations (INGOs) will also be a strong competitive advantage.

Technical Skills and Competencies

Successful candidates should demonstrate the following competencies:

  • Technical Writing: Ability to produce clear, persuasive, and professionally structured documents using international development and humanitarian terminology.
  • Grant and Proposal Development: Ability to prepare concept notes, funding proposals, and project documentation.
  • Results-Based Management: Practical familiarity with logical frameworks, outcome and output pathways, and performance indicators.
  • Research and Analytical Skills: Ability to research funding institutions, analyze donor priorities, and synthesize relevant development data.
  • Communication Skills: Ability to prepare professional presentations, donor briefs, and executive summaries.
  • Editing and Quality Assurance: Ability to review documents and improve their clarity, consistency, and compliance with professional standards.
  • Organizational Skills: Ability to manage multiple responsibilities and meet strict proposal submission deadlines.
  • Independent Working Ability: Capacity to work effectively with minimal supervision in a remote working environment.
  • Cross-Cultural Collaboration: Ability to collaborate professionally with individuals and teams from different cultural and professional backgrounds.

Language Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate fluency in English.

English is the required working language for this assignment, and the selected volunteer should be capable of producing high-quality written documents, communicating professionally, and collaborating with the UNFPA programme team.

Strong written English is particularly important because the assignment involves preparing funding proposals, donor reports, concept notes, and strategic communication materials.

Assignment Duration and Working Arrangements

The assignment will be conducted entirely online, making it possible for the selected volunteer to contribute remotely without relocating to Eswatini.

The main working arrangements include:

  • Duration: 12 weeks.
  • Weekly Commitment: 16–20 hours.
  • Modality: Online.
  • Host Organization: UNFPA Eswatini Country Office.
  • Available Positions: One.

The volunteer will work virtually with the relevant UNFPA programme specialists and other Country Office personnel.

Since the assignment involves competitive funding applications and donor engagement, the selected candidate should be comfortable managing deadlines, organizing independent work, and delivering high-quality outputs within agreed timelines.

Sustainable Development Goal Alignment

This online volunteering assignment contributes to Sustainable Development Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals.

SDG 17 focuses on strengthening global partnerships and mobilizing the financial, technical, and institutional resources necessary to achieve sustainable development.

The assignment directly supports this objective by helping UNFPA Eswatini:

  • Identify potential funding partners.
  • Strengthen institutional resource mobilization.
  • Develop competitive funding proposals.
  • Improve donor engagement and communication.
  • Establish stronger relationships with international development institutions.
  • Secure resources for programmes addressing health, gender equality, and youth empowerment.

Through these activities, the volunteer will contribute to strengthening the partnerships and financing mechanisms needed to advance sustainable development priorities.

Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity Statement

United Nations Volunteers (UNV) is committed to providing equal opportunities to qualified applicants and promoting diversity within its volunteer community.

The programme welcomes applications from qualified professionals regardless of their race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy status, age, language, social origin, or other status.

UN Volunteers are expected to uphold the organization’s values, respect human rights, promote individual dignity, and actively oppose all forms of discrimination.

Application Deadline

Interested applicants should submit their applications before the official closing date.

Application Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 03:00.

Since this is a competitive recruitment process with only one available assignment, interested candidates are encouraged to prepare their applications and submit them before the deadline.

Apply here

How to Apply for the UNFPA Eswatini Online Volunteer Opportunity

Applicants can access the official United Nations Volunteers platform to review the assignment details and submit their applications.

Follow these steps:

  1. Visit the official United Nations Volunteers opportunities portal.
  2. Locate the assignment titled Grant and Proposal Development Support under UNFPA Eswatini.
  3. Carefully review the assignment description, educational requirements, professional experience, and technical competencies.
  4. Prepare an application that clearly demonstrates your relevant academic background, grant-writing experience, proposal development skills, and familiarity with international development.
  5. Highlight any previous experience working with UN agencies, international organizations, NGOs, or development institutions.
  6. Submit your application through the official UNV platform before the application deadline.

Official Application Portal

Applicants should ensure that they are applying for the correct assignment and follow the instructions provided on the official platform.

Please note that the United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing, or recruitment fees. Applicants should disregard any requests for payment claiming to be associated with this recruitment process.

Conclusion

The UNFPA Eswatini Grant and Proposal Development Support Online Volunteer Opportunity 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute to international development through grant writing, resource mobilization, donor research, and strategic communications.

By working alongside the UNFPA Eswatini Country Office, the selected volunteer will contribute to identifying funding opportunities, preparing competitive proposals, strengthening donor relationships, and supporting programmes that address some of the country’s most important development challenges.

The assignment is particularly relevant to individuals with backgrounds in international relations, development studies, public health, economics, gender studies, and other related social science disciplines who possess practical experience in proposal development and institutional resource mobilization.

For professionals interested in working with the United Nations, gaining exposure to international development operations, and contributing to programmes that advance sexual and reproductive health, gender equality, and youth empowerment, this online assignment presents a meaningful professional opportunity.

Interested candidates are encouraged to review the eligibility requirements and submit their applications through the official UNV platform before November 18, 2026, at 03:00.

item.content:encoded:
Introduction

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), through its Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net), is inviting applications from motivated and research-oriented individuals for an exciting online volunteering opportunity focused on biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, environmental sustainability, and sustainable development across Southeast Asia. The initiative, titled Research Support for SE Asia Region – Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services, offers 12 online volunteer positions for individuals who are interested in environmental research, policy analysis, knowledge management, climate change, and natural resource management.

This 12-week international volunteering assignment provides an opportunity to work alongside the BES-Net team in supporting preparations for the Southeast Asia Regional Trialogue, which is tentatively scheduled for the first half of 2027. Selected volunteers will contribute to country-level research, information gathering, stakeholder mapping, and the documentation of successful environmental initiatives and sustainable development practices. Their findings will help inform regional discussions involving representatives from science, policy, and practice communities.

The opportunity is particularly valuable for individuals who want to strengthen their research, analytical, reporting, and information management skills while contributing to an important international environmental initiative. Since the assignment is entirely online, volunteers can complete their tasks remotely and arrange their working hours flexibly according to their availability. Applicants are not expected to follow a fixed daily or weekly schedule.

With 12 available positions and a commitment to promoting biodiversity conservation and sustainable development, this opportunity offers participants the chance to contribute to meaningful research supporting environmental protection and regional cooperation.

About the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is a leading United Nations organization working with governments, communities, and development partners to address global development challenges and create a more sustainable, inclusive, and equitable world.

UNDP recognizes that nature and human development are deeply interconnected. Biodiversity, healthy ecosystems, and natural resources provide essential support for human societies, economies, food systems, and livelihoods. However, increasing environmental degradation, pollution, biodiversity loss, and unsustainable resource exploitation continue to threaten these essential systems.

In response to these challenges, UNDP is placing nature at the centre of development planning and implementation. Its work focuses on strengthening environmental governance, increasing biodiversity finance, supporting sustainable development policies, and promoting solutions that benefit both people and the planet.

Through its global network, technical expertise, partnerships, and extensive sustainable development programmes, UNDP works with countries to develop practical responses to environmental challenges and build a more resilient future.

About the Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net)

The Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) is a capacity-building initiative hosted by UNDP. It supports the connection between scientific knowledge, policymaking, and practical environmental action.

The network promotes collaboration among scientists, policymakers, practitioners, development organizations, and other stakeholders to ensure that biodiversity knowledge is translated into meaningful policies and real-world solutions.

BES-Net’s work is particularly relevant to the development of policies and programmes that address biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, climate change, and sustainable development.

For this particular assignment, BES-Net is preparing a regional initiative designed to bring together different stakeholders from Southeast Asia to explore how scientific evidence and biodiversity knowledge can support effective environmental action.

About the Southeast Asia Regional Trialogue 2027

The central purpose of this volunteering assignment is to support preparations for the Southeast Asia Regional Trialogue, which is tentatively planned for the first half of 2027.

The Regional Trialogue will bring together representatives from three important communities:

  • Science: Researchers, scientists, academic institutions, and biodiversity experts who generate and provide scientific knowledge.
  • Policy: Government institutions, policymakers, and decision-makers responsible for developing and implementing environmental and sustainable development policies.
  • Practice: Civil society organizations, private-sector representatives, community groups, financial institutions, and other stakeholders involved in practical environmental action.

The participating countries are:

  1. Cambodia
  2. Indonesia
  3. Malaysia
  4. The Philippines
  5. Thailand
  6. Viet Nam

The Trialogue will explore how biodiversity knowledge can contribute to practical environmental solutions, strengthen policy implementation, and support sustainable development priorities across the region.

Its discussions will primarily draw on the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) Nexus Assessment. Additional insights will be drawn from the Business and Biodiversity Assessment and the Transformative Change Assessment.

The information gathered by online volunteers will help ensure that regional discussions reflect the realities, experiences, priorities, and environmental initiatives of individual participating countries.

Overview of the UNDP Online Volunteer Opportunity

The selected volunteers will provide research and information-gathering support to the BES-Net team. Their contributions will help develop background materials and knowledge products required for the Southeast Asia Regional Trialogue.

Below are the key details of the assignment:

  • Opportunity Title: Research Support for SE Asia Region – Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
  • Host Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
  • Programme: United Nations Volunteers (UNV)
  • Host Country: Malaysia
  • Assignment Modality: Online
  • Number of Positions: 12
  • Duration: 12 weeks
  • Working Hours: 11–15 hours per week
  • Task Category: Research Data Gathering
  • Expected Start Date: Not specified on the published assignment page.
  • Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 14 – Life Below Water
  • Recruitment Type: Competitive Recruitment
  • Application Deadline: 8 November 2026

Although Malaysia is listed as the assignment country, this is an online volunteering opportunity supporting research across six Southeast Asian countries. Applicants should pay particular attention to the participating-country requirements.

What Will Selected Online Volunteers Do?

The primary responsibility of selected volunteers will be to conduct country-level research and gather relevant information that will support the development of the Regional Trialogue knowledge package.

Each volunteer will be expected to research and organize information relating to the participating country assigned to them.

The assignment involves several important research responsibilities.

1. Research National Biodiversity and Sustainable Development Priorities

Volunteers will conduct targeted research into their country’s environmental policies, biodiversity conservation priorities, and sustainable development strategies.

This will involve reviewing important national documents and identifying the country’s commitments, objectives, and ongoing efforts to protect biodiversity and promote environmental sustainability.

Relevant documents may include:

  • National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs).
  • The latest National Reports submitted to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
  • National environmental policies and strategies.
  • Climate change and sustainable development policies.
  • Relevant government programmes and environmental initiatives.

The purpose of this research is to understand how participating countries are addressing biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, and other environmental challenges.

2. Identify and Document Relevant Environmental Initiatives

Volunteers will identify and summarize country-specific examples of successful environmental initiatives and sustainable development responses.

These may include:

  • Ecosystem restoration projects.
  • Biodiversity conservation programmes.
  • Biodiversity financing initiatives.
  • Sustainable agricultural and production systems.
  • Community-led environmental protection activities.
  • Sustainable natural resource management programmes.
  • Integrated biodiversity and sustainable development projects.

The research should highlight initiatives that demonstrate how governments, communities, businesses, and other stakeholders are responding to environmental challenges.

3. Map Key Environmental Stakeholders

Another important responsibility will involve identifying and mapping organizations and institutions that play significant roles in biodiversity conservation, ecosystem management, and sustainable development.

Volunteers will research relevant stakeholders across different sectors, including:

  • Government ministries and environmental institutions.
  • Research organizations and academic institutions.
  • Civil society organizations and non-governmental organizations.
  • Private-sector companies.
  • Financial institutions and development finance organizations.
  • Environmental networks and other relevant development partners.

This stakeholder mapping will help BES-Net identify organizations and individuals whose knowledge, experience, and activities could contribute to the Regional Trialogue.

4. Identify Economic Sectors Connected to Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services

Volunteers will also examine the economic sectors that have significant relationships with biodiversity, ecosystem services, and sustainable development in their respective countries.

The research may cover sectors such as:

  • Agriculture: Agricultural production, sustainable farming, soil conservation, and food systems.
  • Fisheries: Marine biodiversity, sustainable fishing practices, and aquatic resource management.
  • Tourism: Ecotourism, nature-based tourism, and conservation-oriented tourism initiatives.
  • Manufacturing: Sustainable production, resource efficiency, and environmentally responsible industrial practices.
  • Finance: Biodiversity financing, sustainable investments, and financial mechanisms supporting environmental protection.

The purpose is to understand how different economic activities affect natural ecosystems and how these sectors can contribute to biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.

5. Identify Good Practices, Innovations, and Environmental Success Stories

Volunteers will identify examples of good practices, innovative approaches, and successful environmental initiatives that could provide useful lessons for other countries.

These examples, described in the assignment as “bright spots,” may include government-led, business-led, community-led, or finance-supported initiatives.

The research should identify practical approaches that have demonstrated positive results in areas such as:

  • Biodiversity conservation.
  • Ecosystem restoration.
  • Sustainable natural resource management.
  • Community participation in environmental protection.
  • Sustainable business practices.
  • Innovative biodiversity financing.
  • Climate and environmental resilience.

These examples will help participating countries exchange knowledge, learn from one another, and explore opportunities to replicate successful approaches.

6. Identify Implementation Challenges and Opportunities

Understanding the challenges that prevent countries from achieving their environmental and sustainable development priorities is another important component of the assignment.

Volunteers will investigate barriers affecting the implementation of biodiversity, climate change, and sustainable development policies.

These may include:

  • Limited financial resources for biodiversity conservation.
  • Weak institutional coordination.
  • Gaps in environmental policies and their implementation.
  • Limited access to scientific research and technical information.
  • Insufficient community participation.
  • Unsustainable economic activities.
  • Challenges involving private-sector engagement.
  • Limited capacity and resources for ecosystem restoration.

In addition to identifying challenges, volunteers will highlight opportunities for improving implementation, strengthening partnerships, mobilizing resources, and promoting sustainable environmental practices.

7. Identify Country-Specific Case Studies and Bright Spots

Volunteers will support the identification of relevant case studies and successful examples that can inform regional learning and knowledge exchange.

Particular attention will be given to initiatives involving:

  • Businesses and private-sector organizations.
  • Biodiversity and environmental financing institutions.
  • Community-led conservation projects.
  • Government-led environmental programmes.
  • Innovative sustainable development solutions.

The selected examples should demonstrate practical approaches that could inspire similar initiatives in other Southeast Asian countries.

8. Compile Relevant Research Materials, References, and Contacts

Volunteers will also gather relevant research materials, publications, institutional references, and stakeholder contacts.

These resources will help the BES-Net team connect international scientific findings with the specific environmental realities and national priorities of the participating countries.

The research will be particularly useful in contextualizing findings from the IPBES assessments and ensuring that the Regional Trialogue discussions are informed by reliable country-level information.

Expected Deliverable: One Country Summary Note

At the end of the assignment, each volunteer will be required to submit one concise country summary note.

This document will bring together the research, information, findings, and relevant examples collected throughout the 12-week assignment.

The summary note will follow a Microsoft Word document template containing specific questions provided by the BES-Net team at the beginning of the assignment.

The document will cover the major research areas, including:

  • National biodiversity and sustainable development priorities.
  • Relevant environmental policies and national strategies.
  • Ecosystem restoration and biodiversity conservation initiatives.
  • Biodiversity financing and sustainable production systems.
  • Key environmental stakeholders and institutions.
  • Economic sectors connected to biodiversity and ecosystem services.
  • Successful environmental initiatives and innovative practices.
  • Implementation barriers and opportunities.
  • Relevant case studies and country-specific bright spots.
  • References, research materials, and useful stakeholder contacts.

The final document will contribute to the preparation of the Regional Trialogue knowledge package, background materials, factsheets, case studies, and participant preparation resources.

Orientation, Guidance, and Support for Selected Volunteers

UNDP and the BES-Net team will provide guidance and support throughout the assignment to help volunteers understand their responsibilities and complete their research effectively.

Virtual Briefing and Orientation

At the beginning of the assignment, all selected volunteers will participate in a virtual briefing and orientation session.

The session will introduce participants to the assignment, explain the research objectives, clarify the expected deliverables, and provide guidance on completing the country summary note.

Volunteers will also receive the Word document template containing the specific research questions they are expected to address.

Optional Biweekly Catch-Up Meetings

The BES-Net team will organize optional catch-up meetings every two weeks.

These meetings will provide an opportunity for volunteers to:

  • Ask questions about their research responsibilities.
  • Receive clarification on specific research topics.
  • Discuss challenges encountered during the assignment.
  • Obtain feedback and guidance from BES-Net team members.
  • Share progress and exchange ideas with other volunteers.

Participation in these meetings will be optional, allowing volunteers to manage their time according to their availability.

Individual Support Through Email

In addition to group meetings, volunteers will have access to individual guidance through email whenever they require assistance.

This arrangement will allow participants to seek clarification and receive support throughout the research process.

Flexible Working Arrangements and Online Participation

One of the attractive features of this opportunity is its flexible working arrangement.

The assignment is entirely online, meaning selected volunteers can complete their responsibilities remotely without being required to travel to Malaysia or another participating country.

Volunteers will be expected to dedicate approximately 11–15 hours per week to the assignment over a period of 12 weeks.

However, the assignment does not require participants to follow a fixed daily or weekly schedule.

Instead, volunteers can organize their research activities according to their personal availability and convenience, provided they complete the assigned responsibilities and submit the expected deliverable.

This flexibility makes the opportunity suitable for individuals who want to contribute to an international environmental initiative while managing other personal, academic, or professional responsibilities.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants interested in this UNDP online volunteering opportunity should carefully review the eligibility requirements before submitting their applications.

The assignment is seeking 12 online volunteers from the following Southeast Asian countries:

  1. Cambodia.
  2. Indonesia.
  3. Malaysia.
  4. The Philippines.
  5. Thailand.
  6. Viet Nam.

The country-specific focus is important because volunteers are expected to provide research and information that reflects the national environmental policies, institutions, priorities, and initiatives of their respective countries.

Applicants should therefore pay attention to the participating-country requirement when applying.

Required Experience and Skills

The opportunity is intended for individuals with an interest or background in environmental research, biodiversity, climate change, sustainable development, and natural resource management.

The required experience and competencies include:

1. Research and Information-Gathering Experience

Applicants should have experience in research, policy analysis, or information gathering related to at least one of the following areas:

  • Biodiversity.
  • Ecosystems.
  • Climate change.
  • Sustainable development.

2. Familiarity with National Environmental Policies

Applicants should be familiar with their country’s biodiversity and/or climate-related institutions, policies, programmes, and projects.

This knowledge will help them identify relevant national priorities and gather accurate information.

3. Basic Knowledge of IPBES Processes

Applicants should have basic knowledge of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) processes and assessments.

However, individuals with a strong interest in learning about IPBES and its work may also find this opportunity relevant.

4. Strong Analytical and Synthesis Skills

Applicants should be able to examine information from different sources, identify important findings, organize research materials, and present information in a clear and meaningful way.

5. Independent Working Ability

Since the assignment is conducted remotely and offers flexible working arrangements, volunteers should be capable of organizing their work independently and managing their research responsibilities.

6. Strong Written Communication Skills

Participants must be able to communicate research findings clearly and professionally in writing, particularly when preparing the final country summary note.

Educational Requirements

The minimum educational requirement for this assignment is:

Secondary Education

This means applicants are not required to hold a university degree to meet the stated educational requirement.

However, they should possess the relevant research experience, analytical abilities, environmental knowledge, and writing skills required to complete the assignment successfully.

Language Requirements

English is the required working language for this assignment.

Applicants must demonstrate working knowledge of English to understand the research instructions, communicate with the BES-Net team, and prepare the required research materials.

The following languages are listed as desirable, depending on the participating country:

  • Khmer – Working knowledge desirable.
  • Indonesian – Working knowledge desirable.
  • Malay – Working knowledge desirable.
  • Filipino – Working knowledge desirable.
  • Thai – Working knowledge desirable.
  • Vietnamese – Working knowledge desirable.

Knowledge of the relevant national language can be beneficial when reviewing local policies, national reports, research publications, and other country-specific materials.

Areas of Expertise

The assignment is particularly relevant to individuals with interests or experience in the following professional and academic areas:

  • Climate Change.
  • Environment.
  • Knowledge Management.
  • Research.
  • Reporting.
  • Natural Resources Management.

Applicants with experience in these areas may find the assignment especially relevant to their interests and professional development.

Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)

This assignment contributes to Sustainable Development Goal 14 (SDG 14): Life Below Water.

SDG 14 focuses on conserving and sustainably using oceans, seas, and marine resources for sustainable development.

The opportunity supports this broader objective through research into biodiversity, ecosystem services, sustainable resource management, and environmental initiatives.

Although the assignment covers broader biodiversity and sustainable development issues, its contribution to understanding and protecting aquatic and marine ecosystems makes SDG 14 particularly relevant.

Why Should You Consider This UNDP Online Volunteering Opportunity?

Participating in this assignment can provide several professional, academic, and personal development benefits.

1. Gain Experience Working with a United Nations Development Initiative

Volunteers will contribute directly to research supporting a UNDP-hosted environmental initiative. This provides exposure to international development work and the processes involved in preparing regional environmental discussions.

2. Strengthen Research and Analytical Skills

The assignment provides practical opportunities to conduct policy reviews, collect information, assess research materials, identify stakeholders, and synthesize findings into a structured document.

3. Develop Knowledge of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services

Participants will gain a deeper understanding of biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, environmental policies, sustainable production, and natural resource management.

4. Understand International Environmental Frameworks

Through exposure to the IPBES assessments, National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans, and Convention on Biological Diversity reporting processes, volunteers can strengthen their understanding of international biodiversity and environmental governance.

5. Improve Professional Writing and Reporting Skills

Preparing the final country summary note will provide practical experience in organizing research findings and communicating complex information in a clear and professional manner.

6. Build International Professional Connections

Working with the BES-Net team and other volunteers from participating countries provides opportunities to interact with individuals interested in environmental research, biodiversity, and sustainable development.

7. Contribute to Regional Environmental Cooperation

The information collected will support discussions involving science, policy, and practice communities across six Southeast Asian countries, giving volunteers an opportunity to contribute to regional knowledge exchange.

8. Work Remotely with Flexible Scheduling

The entirely online format allows volunteers to complete their responsibilities remotely, with the flexibility to arrange their working hours around their availability.

Important Information About the Volunteer Assignment

Before applying, interested candidates should understand the nature of the opportunity.

This is an online volunteering assignment under the United Nations Volunteers programme. It is not advertised as a paid employment position.

The UNV description explains that volunteerism involves activities undertaken freely for the public good, where monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that the assignment comes with a salary, employment benefits, or financial compensation.

The assignment requires approximately 11–15 hours of commitment per week for 12 weeks, and the main expected deliverable is one country summary note.

Applicants should also understand that the assignment is specifically designed to support research relating to six Southeast Asian countries. The host entity being listed in Malaysia does not mean the opportunity is open to applicants from every country.

Application Deadline

Application Deadline: 8 November 2026

Interested and eligible candidates are encouraged to review the official assignment details and submit their applications through the United Nations Volunteers online platform before the advertised deadline.

Late applications may not be considered.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow these steps to access the opportunity and submit an application:

  1. Visit the official United Nations Volunteers online platform.
  2. Navigate to the opportunities section.
  3. Search for the assignment titled Research Support for SE Asia Region – Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services.
  4. Carefully review the assignment description, eligibility requirements, experience requirements, and language criteria.
  5. Confirm that your country of residence or nationality meets the participating-country requirements.
  6. Prepare the relevant information about your research experience, environmental knowledge, analytical abilities, and written communication skills.
  7. Complete the application process through the official UNV platform.
  8. Submit your application before the deadline of 8 November 2026.

Official Application Platform Here

Applicants should ensure that they are accessing the genuine United Nations Volunteers website before submitting personal information.

Important Notice to Applicants

The United Nations does not charge applicants any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing, or recruitment fees.

Anyone requesting payment in exchange for access to this opportunity or assistance with recruitment should be treated with caution.

Applicants are encouraged to use only the official UNV application platform and verify the authenticity of any communication claiming to represent the United Nations or UNDP.

Conclusion

The UNDP Research Support for SE Asia Region – Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services online volunteering opportunity presents an important opportunity for individuals interested in environmental research, biodiversity conservation, climate change, and sustainable development to contribute to a meaningful international initiative.

Through this 12-week assignment, 12 selected volunteers will support the Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) in preparing for the Southeast Asia Regional Trialogue scheduled for the first half of 2027. Their research will help document national environmental priorities, identify successful biodiversity initiatives, map important stakeholders, examine economic sectors, and highlight implementation challenges and opportunities across six Southeast Asian countries.

Beyond contributing to regional environmental cooperation, participants will have the opportunity to strengthen their research, analytical, reporting, and professional communication skills while gaining practical exposure to the work of a UNDP-hosted initiative.

With secondary education as the minimum stated educational requirement, flexible online participation, and no fixed daily working schedule, the assignment offers an accessible volunteering format for individuals who meet the country-specific and experience requirements.

Interested candidates from Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Viet Nam should carefully review the official eligibility criteria and submit their applications before 8 November 2026.

This is an opportunity to contribute knowledge, support environmental sustainability, and become part of a collaborative effort to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable development across Southeast Asia.
