item.content:encoded:
Young people aged 15 to 24 who are currently residing in Malaysia are invited to participate in a UNICEF Malaysia initiative focused on creating a Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment. The open call seeks youth leaders who can contribute their perspectives, ideas and experiences to the development of a youth-focused environmental manifesto that will be presented to Members of Parliament.

The initiative provides an opportunity for eligible young people to contribute to discussions about environmental conditions and sustainability, bringing youth voices into conversations with parliamentary representatives. By participating in the co-creation process, selected youth leaders can help articulate young people’s perspectives on the importance of living in a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

The call is specifically directed at young people aged 15 to 24 who reside in Malaysia. Applicants must also be in Malaysia and available to participate on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026. These dates are essential participation requirements, so interested applicants should check their availability before submitting the form.

The application form collects personal and contact information, details about applicants’ residence, Indigenous identity, accessibility or reasonable accommodation needs, and parental or guardian consent for applicants under 18. Applicants should provide accurate information and review the form carefully before submitting their responses.

1. Overview of the UNICEF Malaysia Youth Environmental Manifesto Call

The open call is associated with UNICEF Malaysia and focuses on youth participation in the development of a manifesto addressing a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

Key details include:

  • Organiser: UNICEF Malaysia.
  • Opportunity: Youth participation in co-creating an environmental manifesto.
  • Main focus: A Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment.
  • Target participants: Youth leaders aged 15 to 24.
  • Location requirement: Applicants must reside in Malaysia and be in the country for the required programme dates.
  • Required availability: 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026.
  • Main activity: Collaboratively developing a manifesto and presenting it to Members of Parliament.
  • Application method: Online application form.
  • Application deadline: Not specified in the supplied announcement and form excerpt.

Applicants should rely on the official application form or communications from UNICEF Malaysia for any additional details, including the submission deadline, selection process and further participation requirements.

2. About UNICEF Malaysia

The United Nations Children’s Fund, commonly known as UNICEF, works to advance the rights and well-being of children. UNICEF Malaysia is the organisation identified in this open call as seeking youth leaders to help develop the environmental manifesto.

The initiative is framed around the participation of young people in expressing their views on environmental issues and presenting a shared manifesto to Members of Parliament. It provides a structured opportunity for eligible youth to contribute to a collective statement concerning the environment in which people live, grow and participate in their communities.

The supplied announcement does not provide further information about the programme’s funding, duration beyond the specified dates, venue, number of selected participants or whether travel and accommodation will be provided. Applicants should seek clarification from the organisers if these details are important to their participation.

3. What Is the Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment?

A manifesto is a document that presents a set of ideas, priorities, concerns or proposals around a particular issue. In this initiative, the intended manifesto concerns the creation and protection of a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

UNICEF Malaysia is inviting young people to co-create the manifesto. This means the initiative is intended to involve youth participants in developing its content rather than simply asking them to receive a document prepared by others.

The environmental focus brings together four central ideas:

A. A Safe Environment

The call highlights the importance of a safe environment. The supplied announcement does not define specific safety issues or list particular proposals that the manifesto must address. Applicants can use the application process to learn more about the programme’s intended scope and the topics that participants will discuss.

B. A Clean Environment

Cleanliness is another central element of the proposed manifesto. The initiative’s title identifies a clean environment as one of the outcomes around which youth perspectives will be brought together.

The announcement does not specify whether participants will focus on waste management, pollution, sanitation or other particular issues. Applicants should not assume that any one topic is mandatory unless the organisers provide additional guidance.

C. A Healthy Environment

The call also focuses on a healthy environment. It invites youth leaders to contribute to a manifesto that brings attention to this broad environmental objective.

The supplied information does not provide a detailed health framework or a list of environmental health priorities. The exact issues to be discussed should be confirmed through official programme communications.

D. A Sustainable Environment

Sustainability is the fourth element of the manifesto’s title. The initiative seeks to bring young people’s voices into the development of a shared document on a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

The announcement does not identify specific sustainability targets, policy recommendations or environmental indicators. These should not be treated as confirmed programme requirements unless they appear in the official materials.

4. Why Youth Participation Is Central to This Initiative

The call specifically seeks youth leaders aged 15 to 24. Its main activity is the collaborative development of a manifesto that will be presented to Members of Parliament.

This makes youth participation a defining feature of the opportunity. Young people who are selected will have the opportunity to contribute their perspectives to a document intended for presentation to parliamentary representatives.

The opportunity may be relevant to young people interested in environmental issues, youth leadership, public participation or advocacy. However, the supplied form does not list environmental qualifications, previous advocacy experience or formal leadership credentials as mandatory admission requirements. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a particular qualification or previous project is required unless the full application form states otherwise.

Participation is subject to eligibility, selection and the ability to attend the specified dates. The announcement does not guarantee that every applicant will be selected or that participation will lead to any particular policy outcome.

5. What Selected Participants Are Expected to Do

The announcement identifies two principal activities:

  1. Co-create the environmental manifesto. Youth leaders will contribute to the development of a manifesto centred on a safe, clean, healthy and sustainable environment.
  2. Present the manifesto to Members of Parliament. The initiative includes presenting the completed manifesto to parliamentary representatives.

Applicants must be available on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026 and must be in Malaysia for the programme requirements.

The supplied material does not explain the precise agenda for each date, the expected working hours, the venue or whether all activities will be conducted in person. It also does not provide a detailed description of preparatory work, group assignments, presentation format or follow-up activities. Candidates should confirm these arrangements with UNICEF Malaysia before making travel or scheduling commitments.

6. Eligibility Requirements for Applicants

The announcement establishes several essential participation conditions.

A. Age Requirement

Applicants must be between 15 and 24 years old.

Young people outside this age range are not included in the stated target group. Applicants should provide their correct date of birth in the application form.

B. Residence in Malaysia

The opportunity is intended for youth leaders residing in Malaysia. The form asks applicants to identify both their state or federal territory of origin and their current state or federal territory of residence.

The listed locations are:

  • Johor
  • Kedah
  • Kelantan
  • Melaka
  • Negeri Sembilan
  • Pahang
  • Penang
  • Perak
  • Perlis
  • Sabah
  • Sarawak
  • Selangor
  • Terengganu
  • Labuan
  • Kuala Lumpur
  • Putrajaya

Applicants should select the location that accurately reflects their current residence and separately provide their state or federal territory of origin.

The form’s list identifies Malaysian states and federal territories. It does not provide a separate list of eligible nationalities or explicitly explain whether non-Malaysian citizens who reside in Malaysia may apply. Prospective applicants who are unsure whether their residency status qualifies should seek clarification from UNICEF Malaysia.

C. Availability on the Required Dates

Participants must be available on all three dates specified in the announcement:

  • 14 November 2026.
  • 1 December 2026.
  • 2 December 2026.

Applicants should review their school, university, work and personal commitments before applying. The announcement presents these dates as a participation requirement, so applicants should not assume that missing one date will be permitted.

D. Parental or Guardian Consent for Applicants Under 18

The application form asks applicants under the age of 18 whether they will be able to obtain written consent from a parent or guardian if selected.

Applicants under 18 should be prepared to secure the required written consent if they are chosen to participate. The form offers three responses: Yes, No or Not applicable.

The question is specifically relevant to applicants who are under 18. Applicants aged 18 or older can select the response that corresponds to the form’s instructions.

E. Indigenous Identity

The form asks whether applicants identify as Indigenous. Applicants can answer Yes or No.

The question appears in the personal details section of the application form. The supplied material does not state that Indigenous identity is a condition of eligibility or that only Indigenous applicants may apply. Applicants should answer the question truthfully and should not interpret it as a restriction unless UNICEF Malaysia provides additional guidance.

F. Reasonable Accommodation and Support

Applicants are asked whether they require any reasonable accommodation or support to participate fully in the programme.

If an applicant answers Yes, the form provides a follow-up question asking them to describe the support or accommodation that would help them participate fully.

This gives applicants a way to communicate relevant access or participation needs. Applicants who require support should describe their needs clearly in the designated section. The supplied announcement does not specify which accommodations are available or whether all requests can be provided, so applicants may need to confirm arrangements with the organisers.

7. Information Required in the Application Form

The supplied application form begins with a personal details section. It includes the following questions.

1. Full Name

Applicants must enter their full name. They should use accurate personal details and ensure that their name is entered consistently with relevant identification documents where applicable.

2. Preferred Name

Applicants can provide the name they prefer to be addressed by during the programme.

3. Date of Birth

The form requests the applicant’s date of birth and displays a date-entry format of month/day/year. Applicants should enter the correct date because age is one of the main eligibility requirements.

4. State or Federal Territory of Origin

Applicants select their state or federal territory of origin from the list provided in the form.

5. Current State or Federal Territory of Residence

Applicants identify where they currently reside in Malaysia. This is distinct from their state or federal territory of origin.

6. Email Address

A valid email address is requested so that the applicant can provide contact details. Applicants should use an email account they can access and check regularly.

7. WhatsApp Contact Number

The form requests a WhatsApp contact number. Applicants should enter a correct number and ensure they can receive communications through that channel.

8. Indigenous Identity

Applicants are asked whether they identify as an Indigenous person, with Yes and No options.

9. Reasonable Accommodation or Support

Applicants indicate whether they require reasonable accommodation or support to participate fully.

10. Details of Requested Support

Applicants who answer Yes to the accommodation question can explain what support would help them participate. This question is conditional on the response to the previous question.

11. Written Parental or Guardian Consent for Applicants Under 18

Applicants under 18 are asked whether they can obtain written consent from a parent or guardian if selected. The available responses are Yes, No and Not applicable.

The form also states that personal details such as names and email addresses are not automatically collected unless applicants provide them. It is hosted through Microsoft Forms, and the notice explains that information submitted through the form is sent to the form owner.

The form’s notice also says that the owner has not provided a privacy statement explaining how submitted personal information will be used. Applicants should therefore read the information displayed on the form carefully and contact the organisers if they need clarification about data handling before submitting personal details.

8. How to Apply for the UNICEF Malaysia Youth Environmental Manifesto Call

The supplied material includes the opening page of the application form but does not include a complete public application URL. The form appears to continue across three pages, and the excerpt provided contains the first page.

Interested young people should locate the official UNICEF Malaysia announcement or application form before submitting their details. Once they have accessed the correct form, they should follow the instructions shown on each page.

A practical application preparation process is as follows:

  1. Confirm that you meet the age requirement. Ensure that you are between 15 and 24 years old.
  2. Confirm your residence. Make sure you currently reside in Malaysia and can meet the programme’s location requirements.
  3. Check your availability. Ensure that you can participate on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026.
  4. Prepare your personal information. Have your full name, preferred name, date of birth and residence details ready.
  5. Provide valid contact information. Enter an accessible email address and the correct WhatsApp number.
  6. Answer the Indigenous identity question accurately. Select the response that reflects your circumstances.
  7. Consider any support needs. If you require reasonable accommodation, explain what would help you participate fully.
  8. Arrange parental or guardian consent if applicable. If you are under 18, determine whether you can obtain written consent if selected.
  9. Complete all pages of the form. The supplied excerpt shows page one of three, so applicants should check the remaining pages for additional questions or instructions.
  10. Review your responses before submitting. Confirm that the details are correct and that you have followed the form’s instructions.

Applicants should not assume that completing the form guarantees selection. The supplied information does not describe the selection criteria, notification date, number of available places or whether applicants will be interviewed.

APPLY HERE

9. Application Deadline and Important Dates

The announcement specifies three dates on which participants must be available:

Date Requirement
14 November 2026 Required availability
1 December 2026 Required availability
2 December 2026 Required availability

Application deadline: The supplied announcement and form excerpt do not state a submission deadline.

Applicants should consult the official UNICEF Malaysia announcement or application form for any deadline or additional timeline information. Because the first required date is 14 November 2026, interested youth leaders should check the official application channel promptly rather than assume that applications will remain open indefinitely.

Click HERE for more information about UNICEF Malaysia Youth Call 2026.

10. Is Funding or Financial Support Provided?

The supplied announcement does not state whether participants will receive a stipend, transport allowance, accommodation, meals, reimbursement or other financial support.

It also does not specify whether the programme is free of charge or whether participants must cover their own travel and other costs.

Applicants should contact UNICEF Malaysia or consult the full official programme information to confirm:

  • Whether participation is free.
  • Whether travel costs are covered.
  • Whether meals or refreshments are provided.
  • Whether accommodation is available or funded if required.
  • Whether local transportation support is available.
  • Whether any additional costs are associated with participation.

Candidates should not make financial assumptions based solely on the supplied announcement.

11. Frequently Asked Questions

Who can apply for the UNICEF Malaysia environmental manifesto initiative?

The stated target group is youth leaders aged 15 to 24 who reside in Malaysia and can be present in the country and available on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026.

Must applicants live in Malaysia?

Yes. The announcement specifically states that participants must be residing in Malaysia and must be in the country for the required dates.

Can applicants from outside Malaysia apply?

The call is directed at young people residing in Malaysia. The supplied material does not explicitly specify nationality requirements or confirm whether foreign citizens who live in Malaysia are eligible. Applicants who need clarification should contact UNICEF Malaysia.

What will participants do?

Participants will co-create a Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment and present it to Members of Parliament.

Do applicants need previous environmental experience?

The supplied announcement does not specify previous environmental experience, a particular academic qualification or a minimum level of leadership experience as mandatory requirements.

Can applicants under 18 participate?

The form includes a question asking applicants under 18 whether they can obtain written parental or guardian consent if selected. Applicants in this age group should be prepared to meet this condition.

Is the opportunity specifically for Indigenous youth?

The form asks whether applicants identify as Indigenous, but the supplied information does not state that the opportunity is restricted to Indigenous applicants. It should not be interpreted as an Indigenous-only call without confirmation from UNICEF Malaysia.

Is there an application fee?

The supplied material does not state whether there is an application fee. Applicants should confirm this through the official application channel and avoid paying unofficial intermediaries.

What is the deadline?

No application deadline is visible in the supplied announcement and form excerpt. The programme requires availability on 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026, and applicants should check the official form for submission instructions and any deadline.

Where can applicants find the form?

The supplied excerpt does not contain the complete form URL. Applicants should access it through the official UNICEF Malaysia announcement or a verified UNICEF Malaysia communication.

Conclusion

The UNICEF Malaysia Manifesto for a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment open call offers young people an opportunity to contribute to a collective environmental manifesto and present it to Members of Parliament. By seeking participants aged 15 to 24 who reside in Malaysia, the initiative places youth participation at the centre of a process focused on environmental priorities.

Interested applicants should first confirm that they meet the age and residence requirements and can attend all three required dates: 14 November, 1 December and 2 December 2026. They should also complete the application form carefully, provide accurate contact details, communicate any reasonable accommodation needs and prepare written parental or guardian consent if they are under 18 and selected.

The supplied announcement does not identify an application deadline, funding arrangements or the complete application URL. Prospective participants should verify these details through UNICEF Malaysia’s official channels before submitting their information. Eligible young people who are interested in environmental advocacy and contributing their perspectives to a manifesto for parliamentary representatives should review the full application instructions and apply through the verified official form.

item.content:encoded:
The National Young Farmers Coalition (Young Farmers) Board of Directors Application invites interested individuals to apply for a volunteer leadership position with an organization dedicated to supporting young farmers, strengthening agricultural communities, and addressing the structural and economic barriers that prevent young people from establishing and growing successful farming businesses.

The National Young Farmers Coalition represents, mobilizes, and engages young farmers to help ensure their success. Since its founding in 2010, the organization has developed a grassroots network of more than 200,000 individuals and partner organizations. Through advocacy, community engagement, leadership development, and policy work, Young Farmers seeks to give young farmers the tools they need to become leaders in their communities and build an effective political voice at local, state, and national levels.

The Board of Directors opportunity is intended for individuals interested in contributing to the organization’s governance, strategic direction, advocacy priorities, and long-term impact. Board members volunteer their time, participate in quarterly virtual board meetings, serve on committees, attend an annual in-person board retreat, and contribute to the organization’s wider activities throughout the year.

Young Farmers is particularly interested in maintaining a board with a majority of farmer members, preserving majority representation of Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC), improving representation across regions of the United States, and filling specific expertise gaps. The application specifically identifies a need for individuals with finance and investment expertise and government or legal expertise.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews are scheduled until the available board seats are filled. The supplied application information does not specify a fixed calendar deadline. Interested candidates should therefore review the application form and contact the organization if they need clarification about current vacancies or the recruitment timeline.

Overview of the National Young Farmers Coalition Board of Directors Opportunity

The following table summarizes the key details provided in the application information.

Opportunity detail Information
Organization National Young Farmers Coalition (Young Farmers)
Position Volunteer Board of Directors member
Opportunity location United States; the organization seeks improved representation across US regions
Appointment type Volunteer board service
Term length Two years
Board size 7 to 15 members
Board composition Majority farmer membership
Representation priority Preserve majority BIPOC board membership
Meetings Quarterly virtual board meetings
Committee service Required
Annual retreat Two-day, in-person retreat in January or February
Time commitment At least 2–4 hours per month; up to 10 hours per month during major strategic periods
Other commitments Board education, networking or fundraising participation, and communication between meetings
Recruitment process Applications reviewed and interviews scheduled on a rolling basis until seats are filled
Application method Online Board of Directors application form
Enquiries salima@youngfarmers.org
Fixed application deadline Not specified in the supplied application information

About the National Young Farmers Coalition

The National Young Farmers Coalition is an organization focused on representing and mobilizing young farmers and helping them succeed. Its work addresses the practical, economic, political, and structural challenges that can prevent aspiring and established young farmers from building sustainable agricultural businesses.

Since 2010, the organization has developed a grassroots network of more than 200,000 individuals and partner organizations. This network supports its efforts to strengthen farmer leadership, build community participation, and advocate for policies that address barriers to farming.

Young Farmers works to ensure that farmers have the tools to participate in decisions that affect their livelihoods and communities. Its approach connects grassroots organizing with policy advocacy and leadership development, helping farmers contribute to conversations at local, state, and national levels.

Key issues addressed by Young Farmers

The application identifies several structural and economic barriers that the organization works to address.

Access to affordable farmland: Access to land is a significant consideration for people who want to enter farming or expand an existing farm business. Young Farmers includes farmland access among the major issues affecting the success of young farmers.

Student debt: Education-related debt can affect the financial capacity of individuals seeking to establish farming businesses. The organization identifies student debt as one of the economic barriers it addresses through its broader advocacy work.

Climate change: Changing environmental conditions create challenges for agricultural production and the long-term sustainability of farming. Young Farmers includes climate change among its advocacy priorities.

Healthcare: Access to healthcare is another issue identified by the organization as affecting farmers and their ability to sustain their livelihoods.

Racial inequities: Young Farmers works on racial inequities and highlights the importance of representation, including its commitment to maintaining a board with a majority of BIPOC members.

These issues demonstrate that the organization’s work extends beyond agricultural production. It also focuses on the social, economic, environmental, and policy conditions that influence whether young people can enter farming and build successful businesses.

Advocacy achievements highlighted by the organization

The application describes several examples of the organization’s past advocacy work.

  • Investments in beginning farmer training: Young Farmers reports winning historic investments in training for beginning farmers.
  • Outreach to farmers of color: The organization highlights investments in outreach aimed at farmers of color.
  • Farmland conservation: Its advocacy has contributed to investments in farmland conservation.
  • USDA Farm Service Agency microloan programme: Young Farmers reports that its advocacy for a microloan programme resulted in a programme being available in every county and that it has served more than 30,000 farmers.

These examples illustrate the organization’s focus on addressing practical barriers through policy change, institutional engagement, and support for farmers.

Purpose of the Board of Directors

The Board of Directors provides a leadership and governance structure for the organization. Board members are expected to contribute their knowledge, judgment, time, and professional or community experience to help Young Farmers advance its mission.

The organization maintains a board of seven to fifteen volunteer members, with a majority of members being farmers. This majority-farmer structure is intended to ensure that farmers remain central to the organization’s leadership and decision-making.

The organization also seeks to preserve majority BIPOC representation and address gaps in geographic representation across the United States. In addition, it is looking for expertise that can strengthen its work in particular areas, especially finance and investment, as well as government and legal matters.

Priority areas for board recruitment

The application highlights the following priorities.

1. Maintaining a majority of farmer board members

Young Farmers aims to ensure that farmers make up the majority of the board. This reflects the organization’s focus on representing, mobilizing, and engaging young farmers.

2. Preserving majority BIPOC representation

The organization is working to maintain a board in which Black, Indigenous, and People of Color make up the majority. This is an explicit board-composition priority in the application.

3. Improving representation across US regions

Young Farmers is working to fill regional representation gaps. Applicants from different parts of the United States may therefore be relevant to the organization’s effort to strengthen geographic representation, although the announcement does not specify particular states or regions with current vacancies.

4. Adding finance and investment expertise

The organization identifies finance and investment as an area where additional expertise is particularly needed. Candidates with relevant professional, organizational, or practical knowledge may wish to explain how their experience could contribute to board discussions and governance.

5. Adding government and legal expertise

Government and legal expertise are also identified as priority areas. Applicants with relevant experience may be able to contribute to governance, policy, regulatory, or institutional discussions within the scope of board responsibilities.

The announcement does not state that every applicant must have one of these specialist backgrounds. They are identified as areas of particular need, alongside the organization’s wider priorities for farmer membership, BIPOC representation, and regional coverage.

Board Membership Responsibilities

Joining the National Young Farmers Coalition Board of Directors involves an ongoing commitment rather than occasional participation in meetings. Board members are expected to attend meetings, serve on committees, participate in organizational activities, and maintain communication throughout the year.

The application identifies the following responsibilities.

1. Serve a two-year term

Successful applicants are expected to serve a two-year board term.

Candidates should consider whether they can make a sustained commitment to the organization over this period. Board service requires continuity, participation, and engagement with the organization’s work beyond individual meetings.

The supplied application information does not specify whether extensions or renewals are available after the initial term.

2. Attend quarterly virtual board meetings

Board members must attend quarterly virtual board meetings. These meetings provide a formal setting for board members to discuss organizational matters, participate in governance, and contribute to decisions and priorities.

Candidates should be prepared to set aside time for scheduled meetings and participate consistently.

3. Serve on a committee

Board members are required to serve on a committee. Committee participation provides an opportunity to contribute to specific areas of organizational work between full board meetings.

The application does not provide a complete list of committees or indicate how committee assignments are made. Applicants who need details about available committees may contact the organization.

4. Attend the annual in-person board retreat

Board members must attend an annual, in-person board retreat lasting two days. The retreat takes place in January or February.

The application states that the cost of the retreat is covered as needed. It does not provide a detailed breakdown of which expenses are covered or the process for arranging support, so candidates should confirm the practical arrangements with the organization if selected.

The retreat forms part of the board’s annual engagement and should be considered when assessing availability for the term.

5. Participate in board education events

Board members are expected to participate in educational activities, which may include racial equity training.

These activities support board learning and help members engage with issues relevant to the organization’s mission, leadership, and commitments.

The application does not provide a complete calendar of training activities or specify the number of sessions that will be held each year.

6. Maintain Young Farmers membership

Board members are required to maintain membership in Young Farmers. The application notes that membership is open to farmers and advocates.

Applicants should review the organization’s membership information to understand how membership is obtained and maintained. The supplied form does not state the membership fee or whether any special membership arrangements apply to board members.

7. Encourage participation in a networking or fundraising event

Board members are expected to encourage participation in at least one networking or fundraising event.

This responsibility connects board service with the organization’s wider community engagement and resource-development activities. Board members may be asked to support participation, strengthen relationships, or encourage engagement with events that advance the organization’s work.

The application does not state that each board member must personally raise a particular amount of money.

8. Uphold the Young Farmers Theory of Change

Board members are expected to uphold the organization’s Theory of Change.

The application links to the organization’s mission and vision page, where applicants can learn more about its approach and priorities:

https://youngfarmers.org/about/mission-and-vision/

Candidates should review this material before applying so that they understand the organization’s purpose and can assess whether they are prepared to support its direction.

9. Maintain communication and contribute between meetings

Board work continues outside scheduled meetings. Members are expected to communicate regularly by email, participate in committee work, and contribute to additional tasks throughout the year.

This means applicants should assess not only whether they can attend quarterly meetings but also whether they can remain responsive and engaged between them.

Expected Time Commitment

The application states that board members should be able to contribute at least two to four hours per month, with the time commitment increasing to as much as ten hours per month during major strategic periods.

The expected commitment includes:

  • Attending board meetings.
  • Participating in committee meetings and work.
  • Communicating by email.
  • Contributing to additional tasks between meetings.
  • Participating in board education activities.
  • Supporting relevant networking or fundraising events.
  • Attending the annual two-day in-person board retreat.

The stated monthly commitment is a guide to the expected time required. Applicants should recognize that major strategic moments may require additional involvement.

Because the position is voluntary, candidates should consider how board service will fit alongside employment, farming responsibilities, family commitments, education, or other activities.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The application is intended for individuals interested in joining the organization’s board and contributing to its governance and mission. Young Farmers’ work centres on young farmers and their success, while its membership is open to farmers and advocates.

The organization is especially interested in board composition that maintains a majority of farmers, preserves majority BIPOC representation, strengthens representation across US regions, and adds expertise in finance and investment or government and legal matters.

People considering applying should assess whether they can fulfil the board’s responsibilities and whether their experience, perspectives, and skills could contribute to the organization.

The supplied application does not state a formal age limit, minimum educational qualification, required number of years of professional experience, or a complete list of mandatory professional credentials. Applicants should not assume that a particular degree or years-of-experience threshold applies unless this is specified in the linked board job description or confirmed by Young Farmers.

How to Apply for the National Young Farmers Coalition Board of Directors

Interested candidates should complete the official online Board of Directors application form.

The application itself is available through the organization’s Jotform page.

The supplied application content does not include a direct public URL for the form’s main application page. Candidates should use the official form page from which the application was accessed or contact Young Farmers for the correct application link if needed.

Information requested in the application

The form asks applicants to provide personal, contact, and background information. Fields marked with an asterisk are mandatory.

Applicants should be prepared to provide:

  1. Full name: First name, middle name, and last name.
  2. Pronouns: For example, she/her, he/him, they/them, or other pronouns the applicant uses.
  3. Current address: Street address, additional address line if applicable, city, state or province, and postal or ZIP code.
  4. Email address: A valid email address for communication.
  5. Phone number: A contact telephone number.
  6. LinkedIn profile or personal website: Links that help the organization learn more about the applicant.
  7. How the applicant heard about the opportunity: Options include LinkedIn, an event, social media, the company website, family or a friend, email, a job board, or a staff or board member nomination or recommendation.
  8. Name of the referring staff or board member: Required when the applicant heard about the opportunity through a staff member or board member.
  9. Race or ethnicity: The form explicitly asks applicants to provide this information.

The form also includes navigation and save options. Applicants should complete all required fields and follow the form’s instructions before submitting.

Preparing a strong application

The supplied form excerpt does not include a written personal statement, CV requirement, reference requirement, or a prescribed application essay. Candidates should check the complete form and the linked board job description for any additional instructions.

Before applying, candidates may wish to prepare the following information:

  • A clear explanation of their involvement with farming, agricultural communities, or advocacy, where relevant.
  • Examples of leadership, governance, community engagement, or organizational participation.
  • Relevant experience in finance, investment, government, legal work, or another area that could support the board.
  • Information about their regional background and perspective, where relevant to geographic representation.
  • An understanding of Young Farmers’ mission, Theory of Change, and priorities.
  • Confirmation that they can meet the two-year term and expected monthly time commitment.

These are preparation suggestions based on the responsibilities and priorities described in the announcement; they should not be interpreted as additional formal eligibility requirements.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline and Selection Process

The National Young Farmers Coalition states that applications will be reviewed and interviews scheduled on a rolling basis until the available board seats are filled.

This means that the organization does not present a single fixed calendar deadline in the supplied application text. Instead, recruitment continues as applications are reviewed and vacancies are filled.

Applicants who are interested in serving on the board should review the current application information and submit their applications promptly, particularly if the organization is actively filling available seats.

The supplied information does not specify the number of current vacancies, the dates of interviews, the expected date of appointment, or a detailed selection timetable.

The organization states that interested individuals may contact Salima at salima@youngfarmers.org with questions about the application or opportunity.

Click HERE for more information about National Young Farmers Coalition Board of Directors Application 2026.

Important Information About Race, Ethnicity and Board Representation

The application explicitly states that Young Farmers seeks to preserve majority BIPOC membership on its Board of Directors. BIPOC refers to Black, Indigenous, and People of Color.

The form also asks applicants to provide their race or ethnicity. This is part of the information requested in the application.

The organization’s stated aim to preserve majority BIPOC representation is a board-composition priority. The supplied form does not state that only BIPOC candidates may apply, nor does it provide a complete list of race- or ethnicity-based eligibility restrictions.

The organization also seeks a majority-farmer board and stronger representation across the regions of the United States. Applicants should read the linked board job description and bylaws for further details about board composition and governance.

Review the Board Job Description and Bylaws

Candidates are encouraged to review the governing documents linked in the application before submitting an application.

Board of Directors job description:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1bM0KOHqbRU8Zmkz2PVeN_wvoeoPAdpYj/view?usp=sharing

Young Farmers bylaws:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zxY9H5MAhHK_jQXHR-ewxq23ifPY2Eeb/view?usp=sharing

These resources can provide additional context on the board’s responsibilities, governance arrangements, and expectations for members.

Reviewing the documents can help candidates make an informed decision about whether they can fulfil the commitment and whether their interests align with the organization’s mission.

Conclusion

The National Young Farmers Coalition Board of Directors opportunity offers individuals the chance to contribute to an organization working to strengthen young farmers, improve access to agricultural opportunities, and address the economic, environmental, and structural challenges affecting farming communities.

Board members serve a two-year volunteer term and are expected to participate in quarterly virtual meetings, committee work, an annual in-person retreat, educational activities, networking or fundraising engagement, and regular communication throughout the year. The expected commitment is at least two to four hours per month, rising to as much as ten hours during major strategic periods.

Young Farmers is particularly interested in maintaining a majority-farmer board, preserving majority BIPOC representation, improving representation across US regions, and strengthening expertise in finance and investment as well as government and legal matters.

There is no fixed calendar deadline stated in the supplied application information. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the available board seats are filled. Interested candidates should review the application form, bylaws, and board job description, and contact the organization if they require clarification.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for young people across the Commonwealth to become Wellbeing Champions for the Commonwealth Youth Council’s “Are You Okay?” Campaign, a Commonwealth-wide youth mental health and wellbeing initiative focused on starting conversations, listening to young people, strengthening connections and turning youth voices into meaningful action.

The opportunity is designed for young people who want to make a positive contribution to mental health and wellbeing within their communities. No professional mental health qualification is required. Instead, the Commonwealth Youth Council is looking for young people who care about others, are willing to listen and are committed to helping create respectful and supportive spaces where young people can speak openly about their experiences.

As a Wellbeing Champion, participants will help bring the “Are You Okay?” Campaign into their own communities. Champions are expected to encourage conversations, connect young people, amplify youth voices and contribute to a wider movement seeking to make mental health and wellbeing more visible across the Commonwealth.

The campaign itself grew out of calls made by young people at the 2024 Commonwealth Youth Forum in Samoa, where participants called for stronger action on youth mental health, including better access to services, mental health education, prevention and support. The Commonwealth Youth Council says the campaign responds by creating a Commonwealth-wide space in which young people can speak, be heard and contribute to action.

Wellbeing Champions who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact through the campaign will receive certificates of recognition. The current call closes on 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST. LinkedIn

Application deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

Official campaign page:
Commonwealth Youth Council – Are You Okay? Campaign

About the Commonwealth Youth Council

The Commonwealth Youth Council, or CYC, is the official representative voice of young people across the Commonwealth.

Established in 2013 with support from the Commonwealth Secretariat’s Commonwealth Youth Programme, the Council works to integrate young people into development processes at national, regional and Pan-Commonwealth levels.

Its work focuses particularly on:

  • Youth representation and advocacy
  • Youth empowerment and development
  • Leadership and skills development
  • Connecting youth leaders across countries
  • Creating opportunities for young people to participate meaningfully in decision-making
  • Supporting youth-led responses to shared global challenges

The Council describes itself as representing more than 1.5 billion young people and works to ensure their perspectives are included in policy and development discussions. Commonwealth Youth Council

The Wellbeing Champions opportunity forms part of that wider youth-engagement agenda.

What Is the “Are You Okay?” Campaign?

The Are You Okay? Campaign is a Commonwealth-wide youth mental health initiative built around a simple but important question:

Are you okay?

Its premise is that young people may frequently respond that they are “fine” even when they are experiencing challenges that remain unseen, unheard or unspoken.

The campaign therefore seeks to move beyond simply asking about wellbeing.

According to the Commonwealth Youth Council, it is intended to create spaces where young people can:

  • Speak about their experiences
  • Be listened to
  • Connect with others
  • Help shape meaningful action around mental health and wellbeing

The campaign is not presented simply as an awareness slogan. It attempts to connect conversations with broader youth participation and action.

Why Was the Campaign Created?

The roots of the campaign can be traced to the Commonwealth Youth Forum held in Samoa in 2024.

Young people participating in the Forum called for stronger action on youth mental health.

Among the issues raised were the need for:

  • More accessible mental health services
  • Better mental health education
  • Greater emphasis on prevention
  • Stronger support for young people’s wellbeing

The Are You Okay? Campaign was developed as a response to those calls.

Rather than treating young people simply as recipients of mental health policies, the campaign seeks to involve them directly in conversations and action.

This approach places youth voices at the centre of the initiative.

The Four Pillars of the Are You Okay? Campaign

The campaign is structured around four simple principles:

ASK — Start the conversation.

This is about taking the first step and creating opportunities for honest conversations about wellbeing.

LISTEN — Hear what young people say.

The campaign emphasizes that asking someone about their wellbeing is meaningful only when people are prepared to genuinely listen to the response.

CONNECT — Make support easier to find.

Young people may need connections to communities, networks, resources or appropriate support.

ACT — Turn voices into action.

The campaign seeks to ensure that conversations about mental health contribute to meaningful responses rather than ending with awareness alone.

The four pillars therefore move from conversation to listening, connection and action.

What Is a Wellbeing Champion?

Wellbeing Champions are young people who help bring the campaign into their own communities.

The Commonwealth Youth Council describes them as young people who take the conversation into their communities, connect peers and amplify youth voices.

This means the role is centered on community engagement and peer connection, rather than professional clinical practice.

Champions can help encourage environments in which young people feel more comfortable discussing wellbeing and recognizing that their experiences matter.

The current recruitment call particularly emphasizes three qualities:

Care, listening and commitment.

Candidates do not need to be psychologists, counselors, psychiatrists or other mental health professionals.

Instead, the programme is looking for young people who are willing to engage respectfully with others and support the broader goals of the campaign.

What Will Wellbeing Champions Do?

As a Wellbeing Champion, participants will help take the Are You Okay? Campaign from a Commonwealth-wide initiative into local communities.

The role may involve helping young people:

  • Start conversations about mental health and wellbeing
  • Feel that their experiences are heard
  • Connect with peers
  • Participate in supportive community spaces
  • Share perspectives on the issues affecting their wellbeing
  • Amplify youth voices through the campaign
  • Contribute to locally relevant campaign activities
  • Help turn conversations into broader community action

The campaign language emphasizes creating safe, respectful and supportive spaces for young people to talk, listen and connect.

The exact format of local participation may vary depending on the champion’s community and campaign activities.

You Do Not Need a Mental Health Qualification

One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that applicants do not need a professional mental health qualification.

That means the call is not limited to:

  • Psychologists
  • Medical students
  • Counselors
  • Social workers
  • Public health specialists
  • Mental health professionals

Young people from different academic, professional and community backgrounds may participate.

The Commonwealth Youth Council is explicitly looking for people who:

Care about others, can listen and want to create respectful and supportive spaces.

This makes the opportunity considerably more accessible to young people who may care strongly about wellbeing issues but have not studied psychology, medicine or a related discipline.

A Community Role, Not a Clinical Role

Applicants should nevertheless understand the nature of the position correctly.

Becoming a Wellbeing Champion does not mean becoming a therapist or mental health professional.

The campaign materials describe Champions in terms of:

  • Starting conversations
  • Listening
  • Connecting young people
  • Amplifying youth voices
  • Supporting community engagement

They do not describe Champions as providing diagnoses, therapy or clinical treatment.

This distinction is important.

The role is primarily one of youth engagement, wellbeing advocacy and supportive community connection.

Creating Spaces Where Young People Can Talk

A central idea behind the campaign is that meaningful conversations may help young people feel:

  • Seen
  • Heard
  • Connected
  • Supported

For some young people, talking openly about mental health can be difficult because of:

  • Stigma
  • Social expectations
  • Fear of judgment
  • Lack of trusted spaces
  • Limited awareness of available support

Wellbeing Champions can contribute by making conversations about wellbeing more normal and accessible in their communities.

The emphasis is not on forcing anyone to disclose personal experiences, but on helping create respectful environments where conversations can take place.

Listening as a Core Part of the Campaign

The campaign’s second pillar is LISTEN.

This matters because asking “Are you okay?” without creating space for an honest answer may have little impact.

The campaign therefore emphasizes hearing what young people actually say.

For prospective Champions, this suggests that interpersonal qualities may matter just as much as formal achievements.

Applicants who are patient, compassionate, respectful and able to listen without immediately judging others may be particularly suited to the role.

Connecting Young People

Another campaign pillar is CONNECT.

Mental health and wellbeing support can be difficult for young people to navigate.

The campaign therefore seeks to make support easier to find while building connections among young people and their communities.

Wellbeing Champions may contribute to this by strengthening peer networks and making the wider campaign visible locally.

Again, this does not mean Champions are expected to replace professional services.

Their role is community-oriented and supportive.

Turning Conversations Into Action

The fourth campaign pillar is ACT.

The initiative recognizes that awareness by itself is not necessarily enough.

Young people’s experiences can potentially inform:

  • Advocacy
  • Community activities
  • Youth programmes
  • Policy conversations
  • Future wellbeing initiatives

By participating as a Wellbeing Champion, young people have an opportunity to contribute to a larger Commonwealth conversation about what youth mental health support should look like.

The Wider Are You Okay? Campaign

Wellbeing Champions are one component of a broader campaign.

The official campaign currently includes three major elements.

The PULSE component invites young people to share their experiences anonymously, helping provide a clearer picture of youth mental health across the Commonwealth.

The Wellbeing Champions component mobilizes young people to bring conversations into their communities, connect peers and amplify youth voices.

The campaign also includes a Grand Convening scheduled for 10 October 2026, World Mental Health Day.

Together, these elements combine individual experiences, community action and wider Commonwealth engagement.

Certificates of Recognition

The programme offers an additional form of recognition for active participants.

Certificates of recognition will be awarded to Wellbeing Champions who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact through the campaign.

This is important because the certificate is connected to participation and impact rather than simply submitting an application or being named a Champion.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to engage meaningfully if selected.

What Does “Meaningful Participation” Mean?

The current public call does not provide a numerical threshold or scoring system defining meaningful participation.

Applicants should therefore not assume there is a fixed number of events or hours required unless the Commonwealth Youth Council provides additional instructions after selection.

The wording nevertheless indicates that certificates are intended to recognize Champions who actively contribute rather than simply hold the title.

Participants should therefore approach the opportunity as an active community role.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity could be particularly relevant to young people interested in areas such as youth development, wellbeing, public health, community engagement, advocacy, social development, peer support, education, communications or youth leadership.

It can also suit applicants who simply care deeply about how young people in their communities are doing.

A candidate does not need a long professional résumé.

Based on the call, some of the most relevant personal qualities are:

  • Empathy
  • Ability to listen
  • Respect for others
  • Commitment
  • Interest in youth wellbeing
  • Willingness to engage with communities
  • Desire to create supportive spaces
  • Ability to work constructively with other young people

Formal mental health credentials are explicitly not required.

Academic Qualifications

The current Wellbeing Champion call does not specify a mandatory degree or academic qualification.

Applicants are not told that they must:

  • Be university students
  • Hold a Bachelor’s degree
  • Hold a Master’s degree
  • Study psychology
  • Study medicine
  • Study public health

The central qualification described in the call is commitment to supporting young people and participating responsibly in the campaign.

This makes the opportunity potentially accessible to young people with a wide variety of educational backgrounds.

Professional Experience

No minimum number of years of employment or professional experience is stated.

The call does not require previous employment in:

  • Healthcare
  • Mental health
  • NGOs
  • Community development
  • Youth organizations

Previous volunteering, peer support or community-engagement experience may naturally be relevant, but the published call does not make such experience mandatory.

Is This Opportunity Open Internationally?

The opportunity is framed specifically around young people across the Commonwealth.

The Commonwealth currently consists of 56 independent member countries across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and Americas, Europe and the Pacific.

The call does not provide a separate country-by-country eligibility rule distinguishing citizenship from residence.

Applicants should therefore understand the geographic target as the Commonwealth community, rather than assume it is a completely unrestricted global programme.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

Candidates in different time zones should pay attention to the use of British Summer Time rather than assuming the deadline refers to their local midnight.

Because this is a time-specific deadline, applicants are encouraged to submit before the final hours.

Key Information at a Glance

  • Programme: Are You Okay? Wellbeing Champions
  • Organizer: Commonwealth Youth Council
  • Focus: Youth mental health and wellbeing
  • Geographic focus: Commonwealth countries
  • Role: Community-based youth wellbeing champion
  • Professional mental health qualification: Not required
  • Main activities: Starting conversations, listening, connecting peers, amplifying youth voices and supporting community action
  • Recognition: Certificates for Champions demonstrating meaningful participation and impact
  • Campaign pillars: Ask, Listen, Connect and Act
  • Grand Convening: 10 October 2026, World Mental Health Day
  • Application deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST
  • Official campaign page: https://cycofficial.org/are-you-okay/
  • Application: https://lnkd.in/e5ttrdqQ

Why This Opportunity Matter

Mental health discussions are often framed around professional services, but supportive communities can also play an important role in whether young people feel comfortable speaking about the difficulties they face.

The Are You Okay? Campaign takes a youth-led approach by involving young people directly in starting conversations and identifying what support and action may be needed.

That approach also reflects the broader role of the Commonwealth Youth Council, which works to increase meaningful youth participation rather than simply discussing young people without involving them.

For participants, becoming a Wellbeing Champion offers an opportunity to contribute to a Commonwealth-wide initiative while bringing its goals into a local community.

It may also help young people develop transferable experience in:

  • Youth engagement
  • Advocacy
  • Community mobilization
  • Communication
  • Listening
  • Wellbeing promotion
  • Leadership
  • Peer engagement

However, the most important element of the programme remains its central purpose: helping create communities where young people feel able to speak and know that someone is willing to listen.

Conclusion

The Commonwealth Youth Council Are You Okay? Wellbeing Champions 2026 opportunity invites young people across the Commonwealth to play an active role in strengthening conversations around youth mental health and wellbeing.

The campaign is built around four straightforward principles — Ask, Listen, Connect and Act — and responds to calls made by young people at the 2024 Commonwealth Youth Forum for stronger action on mental health.

Applicants do not need professional mental health qualifications. Instead, the Council is seeking young people who care about others, can listen respectfully and are committed to creating supportive spaces within their communities.

Selected Champions will help bring the campaign into their communities, connect young people and amplify youth voices. Those who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact can receive certificates of recognition.

For a young person interested in wellbeing, youth advocacy, community engagement or simply helping create spaces where people feel more comfortable talking about how they are doing, this is an accessible opportunity to participate in a wider Commonwealth movement.

Applications close on 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST.

Deadline: October 13, 2026

IREX is seeking academic, professional, and regional experts to serve as application readers for the 2027 Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders.

About the Mandela Washington Fellowship

The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the flagship exchange program of the Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI).

In summer 2027, the Fellowship will bring up to 550 accomplished young African leaders to the United States for a comprehensive, executive-style program designed to strengthen leadership skills, build professional networks, and support collaboration between African and American counterparts.

Fellows participate in academic coursework, professional site visits, and structured networking activities. The program focuses on strengthening collaboration in areas including U.S.-Africa trade and economic prosperity, technological innovation, and peace and security.

The Mandela Washington Fellowship is a program of the U.S. Department of State, funded by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX.

Call for Application Readers

IREX is looking for individuals who can review and score applications using established guidelines and a structured scoring rubric.

Over the past twelve years, application readers have helped assess nearly 478,000 applications from 49 sub-Saharan African countries for approximately 7,800 Fellowship places.

Serving as an application reader provides an opportunity to contribute to a fair and merit-based selection process while gaining insight into emerging priorities, challenges, and locally driven solutions across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Readers may also gain valuable exposure to fellowship selection practices, promising African leaders, and key issues affecting the continent.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suited to academics, professionals, and regional experts with expertise in one or more of the Fellowship’s thematic areas:

  • Business and trade
  • Emerging technologies
  • Governance and security

Experience working in Africa or on sub-Saharan African issues is also relevant.

While expertise in these areas is ideal, it is not a requirement to serve as a reader.

Reader Honorarium

Eligible readers may opt to receive a one-time $100 honorarium for their service.

However:

  • U.S. Government employees and contractors are not eligible to receive the honorarium.
  • IREX cannot make international wire payments.
  • Readers receiving the honorarium must have a U.S. bank account in their own name capable of receiving an ACH/direct deposit transfer.
  • Eligible readers who choose to receive the honorarium must submit a completed W-9 form to IREX for tax purposes.
